title: Core restriction for a whiskering cylinder
statement: Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, internal functor simplicial sets and cores of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory, let $\mathcal C$ be a small quasicategory, and let $\eta:K\times\Delta^1\to K$ be a simplicial homotopy whose track $\eta|_{\{k\}\times\Delta^1}$ is an equivalence edge for every vertex $k$ of $K$. For the whiskering cylinder $H_\eta$ of [lem-coef-infinity-precomposition-cylinder], every edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)^\simeq\times\Delta^1$ is sent to an equivalence edge. Thus $H_\eta$ restricts to a simplicial homotopy between the induced precomposition maps on cores.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, together with the edge-and-triangle criterion for equivalences; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Write $u=\eta|_{K\times\{0\}}$, $v=\eta|_{K\times\{1\}}$ and $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-precomposition-cylinder], $H_\eta:D\times\Delta^1\to D$ is a simplicial map with endpoint maps $u^*,v^*$. By the degreewise product and core definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], any edge of $D^\simeq\times\Delta^1$ is a pair $(\alpha,\epsilon)$ with $\alpha:F_0\to F_1$ an equivalence edge of $D$ and $\epsilon:[1]\to[1]$ weakly increasing. The three possibilities for $\epsilon$ are the two constant maps and the identity.

source.place: Construction 1.5.3.1: evaluation; direct degreewise edge classification.

proof.text: For the edge calculation below, an edge $f:x\to y$ in $\mathcal C$ is an equivalence exactly when $[f]$ is an isomorphism in the presented category $h\mathcal C$ of [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus]. Indeed its inverse triangles give $[g][f]=1_x$, $[f][g]=1_y$. Conversely the cited statement represents an inverse to $[f]$ by an edge $g$ and realizes those two equalities by triangles with precisely the edges $(f,g,\operatorname{id}_x)$ and $(g,f,\operatorname{id}_y)$. These are exactly the witnesses in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Consequently, for any triangle with edges $a=01$, $b=12$, $c=02$, if $a,b$ are equivalences, then $c$ is: the cited statement gives $[c]=[b][a]$, whose inverse is $[a]^{-1}[b]^{-1}$. This is a direct categorical calculation from the cited triangle criterion, rather than an additional lemma.

source.place: Section 1.6, Theorem 1.6.6 and the exact-boundary triangle criterion of the cited DAG node; elementary isomorphism calculation.

proof.text: If $\epsilon$ is constant at $t\in\{0,1\}$, the endpoint formula of [lem-coef-infinity-precomposition-cylinder] identifies its image with the edge $\alpha\circ(\eta_t\times\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^1})$. At a vertex $k\in K$, its component is $\alpha_{\eta_t(k)}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], every component of the equivalence $\alpha$ is an equivalence, including this one. Applying the converse direction of that same criterion makes the image edge an equivalence in $D$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4: componentwise test for the two endpoint-constant cases.

proof.text: Let $\epsilon$ be the identity. Fix a vertex $k$ and put $e_k(t)=\eta(k,t)$. Regard $\alpha$ as $A:K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Define a simplicial square $S_k:\Delta^1_r\times\Delta^1_t\to\mathcal C$ by $S_k(r,t)=A(e_k(t),r)$. Restrict it to the $2$-simplex with ordered vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)$: its two coordinate maps $[2]\to[1]$ are $(0,1,1)$ and $(0,0,1)$. Its edge $01$ is $a=\alpha_{\eta_0(k)}$, its edge $12$ is $b=F_1(e_k)$, and its edge $02$ is $c:t\mapsto A(e_k(t),t)$, precisely the $k$-component of $H_\eta(\alpha,\epsilon)$ by the evaluation construction in [lem-coef-infinity-precomposition-cylinder]. The edge $a$ is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]. The track $e_k$ is an equivalence by hypothesis, so $b$ is one too: applying the simplicial map $F_1$ to its inverse and two inverse triangles preserves their faces and degenerate identity edges. Step 2 applied to this triangle makes $c$ an equivalence. Since this holds for every vertex $k$, [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] makes the image edge in $D$ an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4; explicit evaluation-square triangle, with coordinates from Construction 1.5.3.1 (0060).

proof.text: The cases of Steps 3 and 4 exhaust all edges, so the restricted cylinder sends every edge to an equivalence. For any simplex of $D^\simeq\times\Delta^1$, each edge of its image is the image of a source edge, since $H_\eta$ is simplicial. The core definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] therefore puts that image simplex in $D^\simeq$. Degreewise restriction defines a simplicial map $D^\simeq\times\Delta^1\to D^\simeq$, because the operators are inherited from $D$. Its endpoints are $u^*,v^*$ restricted to cores by Step 1. This proves both the asserted edge property and the homotopy on cores. The argument includes empty $K$ and empty $D$: all component and simplex assertions are then interpreted with their usual vacuous quantifiers.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 and the definition of the core: degreewise factorization and endpoint restrictions.
